confirmed.title: Clicking a line of unknown street on a two-street set now keeps every line, and the name typed for that one line overwrites the other lines' known street names, so 'two streets' becomes 'one street' and lot width gets measured along both streets
confirmed.detail: 6b6e37f changed street_lines_after_pick so that a click on a line whose id is None, in a set known to name two streets, returns every line. street_name_after_pick returns own[k] = None for that line, so the plugin asks for a name. Then gordium_rhino applies the typed name to every returned line: `logic.set_street_lines(facts, lines, [name] * len(lines) if name else None)`. The known names (A St, B Ave) are replaced with one name. street_verdict then returns 'one' straight from the names, without checking the geometry, so Lot no longer stops with 'two_streets'. Lot width is then measured as frontage along both rights-of-way, which §325-8 Col. 7 forbids (round 5/6 P0). Before 6b6e37f the click kept only the unnamed lines, so the A St and B Ave names survived and the measuring still stopped with 'two_streets'. This is the same pattern as the round-9 finding in mirror image: a street name ends up on a line nobody named it for. Checked by running the code: on a 90-degree corner a=[[0,0],[100,0]] (A St), b=[[100,0],[100,50]] (None), c=[[100,50],[100,150]] (B Ave), street_verdict gives ('two', None). Click b and type 'B Ave': street_ids becomes ['B Ave','B Ave','B Ave'] and street_verdict gives ('one', None). How it can happen: ids that mix names and None, on a lot whose corner_lot is not True. Today only a hand-edited project file produces that, since project.py never refuses street_ids. A future lookup that names each line would produce it too.
confirmed.evidence: rhino_logic.py:796 `if street_verdict(lines, ids)[0] == "two" and ids[hits[0]]:` ... else `return [list(map(list, line)) for line in lines]`; gordium_rhino.py:1363-1365 `lines = logic.street_lines_after_pick(...ids=facts.get("street_ids"))` / `logic.set_street_lines(facts, lines, [name] * len(lines) if name else None)`; street_lines.py street_verdict: `if named and len([i for i in ids if i]) == len(lines or []): return "one", None`; measure.py:131-134 stops only on stale/two/unsure.
confirmed.pin: New test in packages/design_checker/tests/test_check.py: with lines [a,b,c] on a 90-degree corner and ids ['A St', None, 'B Ave'], run the plugin's pick sequence: street_name_after_pick gives None, then the architect types 'B Ave', then street_lines_after_pick, then set_street_lines with the plugin's ids. Assert that street_verdict(facts['street_line'], facts['street_ids'])[0] != 'one' (it should stay 'two'), and that facts['street_ids'][0] == 'A St'. To make the plugin's ids testable, move the ids it builds into a rhino_logic helper. A check_site pin should also show lot width stays needs review.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give the typed name only to lines whose street is unknown, and keep every known name. Add a rhino_logic helper, e.g. ids_after_pick(lines, old_ids, picked, name), that returns [old[k] if old and old[k] else name for k in range(len(lines))]. It falls back to [name]*len(lines) only when no ids match (matching_ids is None). The plugin calls this helper in place of `[name] * len(lines)`. Then a set known to hold two streets stays two, and the measuring keeps asking.
skeptics: I read the code and ran the scenario, and the core claim holds. In rhino_logic.py:795, 6b6e37f added `and ids[hits[0]]`, so clicking a line with no street name, in a set whose verdict is "two", now falls through to line 798 and returns every line. street_name_after_pick (rhino_logic.py:746-749) returns own[k] = None for that line, so the plugin asks the architect for a name. gordium_rhino.py:1363-1365 then calls `set_street_lines(facts, lines, [name] * len(lines))`, which puts that one name on all the returned lines. In street_lines.py:74-75, street_verdict returns "one" when every line is named the same, and it does that before any geometry check (heading_change). measure.py:120-135 stops only on stale, two or unsure, so lot width would be measured along both streets. I ran a=[[0,0],[100,0]] 'A St', b=[[100,0],[100,50]] None, c=[[100,50],[100,150]] 'B Ave'. The verdict was ('two', None) and the name lookup gave None. After the pick the result was all 3 lines with street_ids ['B Ave']*3, and the verdict became ('one', None). Two corrections. (1) The finding gets the old behaviour slightly wrong. Before 6b6e37f the click kept only the unnamed line b, named it, and measured along that one line. It did not stop with two_streets. Still, it never measured across both streets, so this is a real regression. (2) It is hard to reach today. Every pick path in the plugin writes the same name on every line or no names at all (gordium_rhino.py:1343 and 1365), and suggested_facts sets no names. So ids that mix names and None come only from a hand-edited project file or a future lookup that names each line. The finding says this itself. The code path is real and gives a false "one street" across a corner, so the finding is not refuted, though its P1 severity is debatable given how hard it is to reach.

I could not refute it. I read the code and ran the scenario, and the finding holds.

**The code does what the finding says.**
- rhino_logic.py:795-798: 6b6e37f added `and ids[hits[0]]` to the "two streets" branch. A click on a line whose id is None now falls through to `return` every line. Before 6b6e37f, `mine = None` kept only the lines with id None.
- street_name_after_pick, rhino_logic.py:746-749, returns `own[k]`, which is None for that line, so the plugin asks for a name.
- gordium_rhino.py:1363-1365 then writes `[name] * len(lines)` over every returned line.
- street_lines.py:71-75 street_verdict returns 'one' when every line has the same name. It does not look at the geometry.
- measure.py:121-134 stops only on stale, two or unsure, so Lot width is measured along both streets.

**Running it confirms this.** With ids = ['A St', None, 'B Ave'], street_verdict gives ('two', None). Clicking b and typing 'B Ave' gives street_ids ['B Ave', 'B Ave', 'B Ave'], and street_verdict now gives ('one', None).

**This path is reachable.** gordium_rhino.py:1333 sends corner_lot True to the multi-pick branch, so this single-pick branch runs only when corner_lot is not True, which is exactly where measure.py checks the verdict.

**It is a regression, not a pre-existing issue.** On the parent of 6b6e37f the same click kept only line b, so the A St and B Ave names were never overwritten and 'two_streets' still stopped the measuring.

**Caveat that lowers the practical severity:** today, mixed name/None ids come only from a hand-edited project file. Normal flows never write them: check.py:831 writes one id, set_street_lines writes all-same or none, and project.py:59 does not refuse street_ids. The finding says this itself. The mechanism is real all the same, and it is a false pass under principle 4.

confirmed.title: street_lines_after_pick keeps the clicked street's lines by exact string match, but street_verdict compares names after normalising them, so a different spelling of the same street gets dropped (fewer street lines on a guess)
confirmed.detail: street_verdict decides 'two' by comparing _norm'd names (case and dots ignored). Picking the street's own lines uses plain `ids[k] == mine`. So ids ['A St','a st.','B Ave'] count as two streets (A St and B Ave). Clicking the 'A St' line returns only [a]: line b ('a st.', the same street) is dropped and the front yard is measured from part of the street. Round 3 F4 called that exact outcome a false pass, and the docstring promises 'never fewer on a guess'. Checked by running it: street_lines_after_pick([a,b,c], a, ids=['A St','a st.','B Ave']) gives [a]. As in the first finding, mixed spellings come only from hand-edited or future per-line ids. The comparison was added on this branch (b96cd1b).
confirmed.evidence: rhino_logic.py:797-798 `mine = ids[hits[0]]` / `return [... for k, line in enumerate(lines) if ids[k] == mine]`; street_lines.py: `named = {_norm(i) for i in ids or [] if i}` and `def _norm(name): return " ".join(str(name).lower().replace(".", " ").split())`
confirmed.pin: test_check.py: assert logic.street_lines_after_pick([a,b,c], a, ids=['A St','a st.','B Ave']) == [a,b]
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compare names with the same normalising that street_verdict uses. Expose street_lines' _norm (e.g. as a public same_street(x, y) helper) and keep line k when same_street(ids[k], mine), so the box and the measuring decide 'same street' by one rule.
skeptics: I could not refute it, and I reproduced it. In rhino_logic.py:794-797, street_lines_after_pick first calls street_verdict(lines, ids). Then it keeps only the lines where ids[k] == mine, which is a raw string comparison. street_verdict (model_measurement/street_lines.py:71-73) counts streets by name after passing each name through _norm (line 82), which ignores case and dots. Nothing in between makes the spellings match. matching_ids (street_lines.py:58-64) only checks the list length and that each entry is a string or None; it does not normalise the names. So ['A St','a st.','B Ave'] is judged 'two' streets (A St and B Ave), but the filter treats 'a st.' as a different name from 'A St'. I ran street_lines_after_pick([a,b,c], a, ids=['A St','a st.','B Ave']) on the branch and got [[[0,0],[10,0]]], only line a. Line b belongs to the same street and is dropped, which is the 'fewer lines on a guess' the docstring rules out. This is new on the branch: `ids[k] == mine` does not appear in eb627d4's rhino_logic.py. No other code in packages compares the names this way. It only matters when one street's lines carry differently spelled names (hand-edited or future per-line ids), as the finding itself says, but the inconsistency in the code is real.

I could not refute this. The two places really do compare street names differently. In rhino_logic.py:793-798, street_lines_after_pick only narrows the picked lines when street_verdict(lines, ids) returns "two". It then keeps the lines where `ids[k] == mine`, a plain string match. street_verdict is in model_measurement/street_lines.py:67-75. It builds `named = {_norm(i) ...}`, and _norm (street_lines.py:82-83) lowercases names and turns dots into spaces before comparing. So with ids ['A St','a st.','B Ave'], street_verdict sees two streets (a st and b ave). The pick filter then keeps only the line spelled exactly 'A St' and drops 'a st.', which is the same street. I ran it: street_lines_after_pick([a,b,c], a, ids=['A St','a st.','B Ave']) returned only [a]. That breaks the docstring's promise of "never fewer on a guess" and repeats the round-3 F4 outcome (front yard measured from part of the street). matching_ids (street_lines.py:58-64) checks only the list length and that each entry is a string or None. It does not normalise spellings, so nothing upstream prevents this. The code is new on this branch: b96cd1b is in eb627d4..HEAD. How likely it is in practice is limited, as the finding admits. check.py:831 builds street_ids from a single capitalised outline street. rhino_logic.py:224 stores ids it is given. So mixed spellings need hand-edited facts or future per-line ids. P2 severity fits.

priorStatus.title: Picking one street of two keeps the street name of the whole set of lines, so a B Ave line gets saved as 'A St'. Clicking an unnamed line keeps only the unnamed lines
priorStatus.reasoning: The reported case is fixed. When matching_ids holds, street_name_after_pick returns the clicked line's own id (verified: clicking c with ids ['A St','A St','B Ave'] gives 'B Ave' and keeps [c]). The second half of the fix is the shallow part: clicking an unnamed line now keeps every line, while the plugin still gives the one typed name to every kept line (`[name] * len(lines)`). So the A St and B Ave lines get renamed to whatever is typed for the unknown line. That is the same defect pattern (a name carried to lines it wasn't given for). It is now worse, because uniform names make street_verdict return 'one' and drop the 'two_streets' stop (finding 1). The new test only checks street_lines_after_pick's return value, not the plugin's name-then-lines-then-set_street_lines sequence.
